label: rem:borromean-word-selection
title: What fixes the Borromean word
html:
The Borromean observable takes the word \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} as input. Two results fix it.

Zero pairwise linking forces writhe 0. At writhe 0 the crossing energy of a word is its length times (q - q^{-1})/2, so for q > 1 minimising the crossing energy is minimising length. By the minimality theorem, the words of least energy among non-trivial pure zero-linking three-braids are exactly the conjugates of \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}. Minimising crossing energy therefore selects the word up to conjugacy.

The Wedderburn form of the Markov trace of a writhe-0 three-strand word depends on the word only through \chi_{(2,1)}. By the character theorem, no other conjugacy class at writhe 0, of any length, shares the value of \chi_{(2,1)} with \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} at q = i and q = 2. So the trace seen by the mass identity does not leave room for a second word.
